ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Cardiology Consultation — Dwight D. Eisenhower — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Two-week blood pressure and kidney check, echocardiogram, and cardiology consultation

text.paragraph: Anterior myocardial infarction about four months ago, treated out of state with a drug-eluting stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery. Please establish local cardiology care, reassess left ventricular function, and advise on his return to full-time work and on the duration of antiplatelet and beta-blocker therapy. [S]
Urgency: Routine, within two weeks; echocardiogram booked for the same morning. [S]

list.item: Has his left ventricular function recovered, and is a defibrillator evaluation needed?
Is he fit to return to full-time work and to fly, and is any further testing needed first?
Do you agree with twelve months of aspirin and ticagrelor, then aspirin alone?
How long should the beta-blocker continue?
Do you agree with an LDL goal below 55 mg/dL with ezetimibe added?

text.paragraph: Mr. Eisenhower is seen at the request of Dr. Okonkwo to establish cardiology care about four months after an anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction treated with a drug-eluting stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery at an out-of-state hospital. He presented late, more than a day after the pain began. He has completed cardiac rehabilitation and walks 40 minutes most days without angina, breathlessness, palpitations, or presyncope. He has not used nitroglycerin. He tolerates all his medicines, with forearm bruising only. He wants to return to full-time executive work, including air travel. [S]
Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Dwight D. Eisenhower was born on October 14, 1890, in Denison, Texas, to David Jacob and Ida Elizabeth (Stover) Eisenhower. [D]
During his war years Eisenhower smoked about four packs of cigarettes a day; he quit, essentially cold turkey, around 1949 at a doctor's suggestion. [D]

On September 23, 1955, during a working vacation in Denver, Eisenhower played golf at Cherry Hills; chest pain woke him early on September 24, an electrocardiogram taken by a cardiac specialist from Fitzsimons Army Hospital confirmed a heart attack, and he was admitted to Fitzsimons that day. [D]

The electrocardiogram recorded an anterolateral acute myocardial infarction with ST-segment elevation. During the golf game he had complained of what he took to be indigestion, and he was hospitalized more than 24 hours after his symptoms began. [D]
Eisenhower remained at Fitzsimons Army Hospital from September 24 until his discharge on November 11, 1955. [D]

list.item: Anterior myocardial infarction about four months ago (I25.2). Left ventricular function has largely recovered: ejection fraction 52 percent with mild apical hypokinesis and no thrombus or aneurysm. A defibrillator evaluation is not indicated. The reassessment was due about 40 days after the infarction and is late, but the result does not change management. [S]

Single-vessel coronary artery disease after stenting (I25.10). Complete revascularization of the culprit vessel, no angina, and 9 METs without ischemia at the end of rehabilitation. He is at low risk, and further stress testing before returning to work would not add information. [S]

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). LDL cholesterol 78 mg/dL on atorvastatin 80 mg. He is at very high risk (recent acute coronary syndrome, age over 65, hypertension, prior PCI), so an LDL goal below 55 mg/dL is appropriate. [S]
Essential hypertension (I10). Blood pressure 128/78 mmHg today on metoprolol and lisinopril 10 mg; potassium and creatinine acceptable two weeks after the increase. [S]

text.paragraph: Data reviewed: Outside angiography and PCI report, the hospital echocardiogram (ejection fraction 45 percent), the cardiac rehabilitation exit test, the intake ECG and laboratory results, and today's transthoracic echocardiogram and basic metabolic panel. [S]

list.item: Return to full-time work now, building up over the first week, and resume air travel; walk during long flights. [S]
Continue aspirin 81 mg and ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily to twelve months after the infarction, then stop ticagrelor and continue aspirin for life. Do not interrupt either drug for minor bleeding. [S]
Continue metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily for at least the first year and reassess then; with hypertension it is reasonable to continue it long term. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 80 mg with ezetimibe 10 mg; recheck lipids in 4 to 12 weeks and aim for LDL cholesterol below 55 mg/dL. [S]
Continue lisinopril 10 mg with a basic metabolic panel every six months. [S]
No routine stress testing or repeat echocardiography unless symptoms change. [S]
Continue home exercise of at least 150 minutes a week; golf is fine. [S]
Discussed with Dr. Okonkwo by telephone today; the patient agrees with the plan. [S]

Follow-up: Primary care will manage monitoring on the CMID schedule and make the antiplatelet change at one year. Cardiology will see him again for angina, breathlessness, palpitations, syncope, or any question about therapy. [S]
